questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.topic: Period of a mass-spring oscillator
questions.learningObjective: Compute period of a mass-spring system
questions.stem: A 0.5 kg mass on a spring of constant 200 N/m oscillates; what is the period in seconds?
questions.explanation: T = 2pi sqrt(m/k) = 2pi sqrt(0.5/200) = 0.314 s. The tempting error is to use sqrt(k/m).
questions.hint: Use 2pi times sqrt of mass over spring constant.

questions.hint: Use 2pi times sqrt of length over g.

questions.topic: Period does not follow amplitude

questions.stem: For an ideal simple pendulum, how does the period change if the amplitude is doubled (small angles)?

options.text: It stays the same, because period is amplitude-independent for small angles
It doubles, because larger swings take longer
It halves, because larger swings are faster
It quadruples, because energy scales as amplitude squared

questions.explanation: For small angles the period is independent of amplitude. The distractors assume amplitude scaling or confuse energy with period.
questions.hint: Small-angle period does not depend on amplitude.

questions.stem: A mass-spring system and a simple pendulum have the same period; if the mass is doubled, which period changes?

options.text: Only the spring period changes, increasing by sqrt(2)

questions.explanation: Spring period depends on mass (T = 2pi sqrt(m/k)), while pendulum period does not depend on mass. Doubling mass multiplies spring period by sqrt(2). The distractors misassign mass dependence.

questions.stem: A mass-spring system has m = 0.4 kg and k = 160 N/m; what is its resonant angular frequency in rad/s?
questions.explanation: omega_0 = sqrt(k/m) = sqrt(160/0.4) = 20 rad/s. The tempting error is to use sqrt(m/k).
questions.hint: Take sqrt of spring constant over mass.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.topic: The defining condition of simple harmonic motion
questions.learningObjective: Apply the SHM condition to identify motion
questions.stem: A particle's acceleration is a = -25 x (SI units); is this SHM, and what is omega?

options.text: No, because acceleration is not constant
No, because the coefficient is negative

questions.explanation: a = -omega^2 x with omega^2 = 25, so omega = 5 rad/s and the motion is SHM. The distractors misread the relation.
questions.hint: Match a = -omega^2 x.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.topic: What sets the amplitude
questions.learningObjective: Compute amplitude from initial conditions
questions.stem: A mass-spring oscillator starts from rest at displacement 0.3 m; what is its amplitude in metres?
questions.explanation: Starting from rest at 0.3 m means the amplitude is 0.3 m. The tempting error is to double it.
questions.hint: Amplitude equals initial displacement when starting from rest.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.topic: What changes a period
questions.learningObjective: Predict period change when spring constant changes
questions.stem: If the spring constant of a mass-spring system is quadrupled, how does the period change?

options.text: It stays the same, because period is mass-dependent only
It quarters, because T is proportional to 1/k
It doubles, because stiffer springs are slower
It halves, because T is proportional to 1/sqrt(k)

questions.explanation: T = 2pi sqrt(m/k), so quadrupling k halves T. The distractors mis-scale or ignore k.
questions.hint: Period is inversely proportional to sqrt(k).

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.topic: Speed and acceleration at equilibrium
questions.learningObjective: Compute speed at equilibrium from energy
questions.stem: A mass-spring oscillator has total energy 8 J and mass 2 kg; what is its speed at equilibrium in m/s?
questions.explanation: At equilibrium all energy is kinetic: 0.5*m*v^2 = 8, so v = sqrt(16/2) = sqrt(8) = 2.828 m/s. The tempting error is to use total energy as 0.5*k*A^2.
questions.hint: Set kinetic energy equal to total energy.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.topic: Speed and acceleration at a turning point
questions.learningObjective: Compute acceleration at a turning point
questions.stem: An oscillator has omega = 5 rad/s and amplitude 0.1 m; what is the acceleration magnitude at a turning point in m/s^2?
questions.explanation: At a turning point, x = A, so a = omega^2 * A = 25*0.1 = 2.5 m/s^2. The tempting error is to use omega*A.
questions.hint: Multiply omega squared by amplitude.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.topic: Period of an off-resonance drive
questions.learningObjective: Compute driven frequency period
questions.stem: A driven oscillator is driven at 10 Hz; what is the period of the steady-state motion in seconds?
questions.explanation: Period = 1/f = 1/10 = 0.1 s. The tempting error is to use the natural period.
questions.hint: Take the reciprocal of the driving frequency.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.topic: Node spacing on a standing wave
questions.learningObjective: Compute node spacing for new wavelength
questions.stem: A standing wave has wavelength 1.2 m; what is the distance between adjacent nodes in metres?
questions.explanation: Adjacent nodes are half a wavelength apart: 1.2/2 = 0.6 m. The tempting error is to use the full wavelength.
questions.hint: Divide wavelength by 2.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.topic: Length needed for a given pendulum period
questions.learningObjective: Compute length for a new target period
questions.stem: What length in metres gives a simple pendulum a period of 1.0 s? (g = 9.8)
questions.explanation: L = g (T/(2pi))^2 = 9.8*(1/(2pi))^2 = 0.248 m. The tempting error is to multiply by T.
questions.hint: Square the period over 2pi, then multiply by g.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.topic: Wave speed on a stretched string
questions.learningObjective: Compute wave speed for new tension and density
questions.stem: A string has tension 400 N and linear density 0.04 kg/m; what is the wave speed in m/s?
questions.explanation: v = sqrt(T/mu) = sqrt(400/0.04) = 100 m/s. The tempting error is to divide without sqrt.
questions.hint: Take sqrt of tension over linear density.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.topic: Period of a mass on a spring
questions.learningObjective: Compute period for a new mass-spring system
questions.stem: A 0.8 kg mass on a spring of constant 320 N/m oscillates; what is the period in seconds?
questions.explanation: T = 2pi sqrt(m/k) = 2pi sqrt(0.8/320) = 0.314 s. The tempting error is to use sqrt(k/m).
questions.hint: Use 2pi times sqrt of mass over spring constant.
